summary.title: The One Key to Dealing with Senior Executives: Answer the Question!
summary.one_liner: Answering the question asked, briefly and directly, is the most important habit when talking with senior executives, and short hedged answers leave room for follow-up.
keywords: how to answer questions from the c-suite
takeaways: Senior executives want direct answers to their questions, so answer what was asked before anything else.
Keep answers succinct; executives often have a line of questioning prepared and want to move quickly.
Use simple hedging such as 'Yes, mostly' or '7, but one or two key problems' to leave a thread for follow-up without disclaimers.
Avoid giving unrequested presentations to senior executives, since they want to drive the agenda.
Track in meetings how often people actually answer the question to build the habit.
summary.summary: This short blog post by Kellblog argues that the most important skill when dealing with senior executives is answering the question they asked. The author describes common executive traits: they are direct, fast, want to control the agenda, and have prepared questions. He contrasts bad answers full of filler and disclaimers with good and best answers using examples such as a team rating on a 1-10 scale and project deadline tracking. The piece is opinion and anecdote rather than a technical guide.
